state.case_summary:
A 58-year-old woman presented with a 3-year history of a right-breast lump. She had no family history of breast cancer, had been menopausal for 5 years, denied eating frogs or snakes, but recalled drinking impure water. On examination, she reported migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant, and a mobile lump was palpated.  
Breast ultrasonography using a 13-MHz transducer revealed:  
- Upper-outer quadrant: a hypoechoic, tubular structure with surrounding increased echogenicity, measuring 5.0 × 1.7 × 0.7 cm (BIRADS 4b)  
- At 6 o’clock: an oval, low-echo mass with well-delineated contours, measuring 1.8 × 1.2 × 0.4 cm (BIRADS 4a) and closely abutting the pectoralis major  
- At 11–12 o’clock: two small hypoechoic masses in the fat layer, measuring 0.5 × 0.3 cm and 0.3 × 0.2 cm  
No obvious blood-flow signals were detected within any of these lesions on color Doppler flow imaging.
